The real question is not whether a system can produce admirable behavior under favorable conditions. The real question is what that same system permits, excuses, or glorifies when authority demands harm. That's the test. If a system can produce generosity one day and justify cruelty the next without changing its core logic, then generosity was never the foundation. Obedience was. If a system can inspire service when the command is beautiful and also demand harm when the command is ugly, then what it is trained is not ethical discernment, it is trained compliance. And a system that calls cruelty good when authority commands it does not understand goodness. It understands hierarchy. That's why compliance is so deceptive. It can wear the clothing of virtue for a long time. It can look humble, patient, loyal, disciplined, and even loving up until the moment it starts harming people. When you stop asking whether something is good and only asking whether God wills it, goodness starts to disappear. Not because the language of goodness goes away, but because the substance of goodness has been replaced by authorization. Compliance can look virtuous right up until it becomes cruel.
